subject.title: feat(slack): Support Slack RTS (Real-Time Search) API via assistant action tokens

question: Should OpenClaw add Slack RTS as a separate assistant action-token search path, and what token containment, scope, and privacy rules should it use relative to legacy user-token `search.messages` work?
rationale: The feature is plausible and aligned with Slack channel improvement, but it handles event-scoped Slack action tokens and workspace search results, so automation should not choose the security/product contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve Narrow RTS Contract
options.body: Implement `assistant.search.context` inside the Slack plugin with event-scoped action-token containment, redaction, rate-limit handling, docs, tests, and live Slack proof.

options.title: Consolidate Slack Search
options.body: Define one Slack search contract covering RTS and user-token `search.messages`, then land a focused current-main PR that preserves read-target authorization and least privilege.

options.title: Defer Workspace Search
options.body: Keep Slack workspace search out of core until maintainers are ready to own the token, privacy, scope, and validation burden.

recommendation.title: Approve Narrow RTS Contract
recommendation.body: Implement `assistant.search.context` inside the Slack plugin with event-scoped action-token containment, redaction, rate-limit handling, docs, tests, and live Slack proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle is the strongest current routing candidate from recent Slack assistant lifecycle, action-runtime, docs, and closed action-parity history.
